description: Solo entry by Rani Gouli (1st-year CSE student) building an interactive Lunar Outpost & Cyber Telemetry Mission Control dashboard using Python, Streamlit, Pandas, and live NASA NEO data.
summary: Project Artemis Mission Shield is an interactive, real-time Lunar Outpost Mission Control and Cybersecurity Telemetry simulator built with Python, Streamlit, Pandas, and live NASA Near-Earth Object (NEO) API data. Developed for the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge, the platform places trainees in command of a lunar habitat where they must dynamically balance interconnected life-support resources—Oxygen, Power, Food Supply, Radiation Shielding, and Communications—while monitoring real-time deep-space asteroid telemetry. Alongside resource trade-offs that compute a live Mission Performance Score (0–100), it features an integrated Cybersecurity Monitoring Center with threat diagnostics, timestamped incident logging, and downloadable CSV audit reports. This dual focus is critical because future Artemis astronauts and students must understand not only how environmental and resource constraints affect lunar survival, but also how cyber resilience protects vital life-support infrastructure in deep space.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

Project Artemis Mission Shield is an interactive Lunar Outpost Mission Control & Cybersecurity Telemetry simulator built for the "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge. Trainees manage a simulated Artemis lunar habitat in real time by adjusting five critical survival subsystems—Oxygen Supply, Power Level, Food Supply, Radiation Shielding, and Communication Signal—while receiving live Near-Earth Object (NEO) asteroid telemetry from NASA's NeoWs REST API. Each resource decision dynamically recalculates a live Mission Performance Score (0–100) and triggers immediate life-support warnings when thresholds become critical.

Creativity & Cybersecurity Integration:

Unlike standard educational space apps that focus solely on environmental survival, Artemis Mission Shield integrates a dedicated Cybersecurity Monitoring Center. Trainees run system integrity checks, log simulated cyber and telemetry anomalies with timestamps, and export both mission telemetry snapshots and cybersecurity audit logs as downloadable .csv reports.

Tools, Languages & Resources Used:

* Language & Libraries: Python 3, Streamlit, Pandas, Requests, Datetime

* UI/UX: Custom CSS deep-space starfield interface and dark telemetry theme

* Data Source: NASA Near-Earth Object Web Service (NeoWs API)

* AI Assistance Disclosure: AI tools were used during development to assist with CSS starfield styling, API error-handling structure, and documentation formatting.
